verdict.rationale: Lium's own docs and CLI cover most of the agent lifecycle without a console. An agent can provision a pod with `lium up --gpu H100 --ttl 1h` or rent-by-spec via the API, run workloads with `lium exec` (which returns the remote exit code) or the SDK, and tear down through explicit removal, TTL, or spend-cap auto-deletion; the agents doc states this all works with no browser. Monitoring a running pod's status and health is only thinly evidenced: `lium spend` reports cost per pod, and the WebSocket covers marketplace availability rather than pod health. The OpenAPI probe at docs.lium.io returned 404, though the docs point to a spec at lium.io/api/openapi.json. Missing for 10: documented pod status/health/utilization monitoring via API, CLI or MCP; an MCP server that manages pods (the documented one only covers docs and prices); independent hands-on corroboration of the end-to-end agent flow.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can provision a GPU, monitor it, run a workload, and tear it down end to end through documented APIs, CLI, or MCP without a human in the console

citations.quote: An agent can do everything on Lium with no browser: sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods.
lium exec job "nvidia-smi"                              # exits with the remote command's exit code
The SDK rents the cheapest matching node, runs the function there, returns the result and removes the pod (or keeps it warm).
rent-by-spec (`POST /executors/rent-by-spec`) that rents the cheapest node matching a GPU spec under a `max_price_per_gpu_hour` ceiling
lium spend                                     # burn per hour, spend per pod, runway
